style: Read clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace
lines: This is an air track. The gliders ride on air, so almost nothing slows them down. Set the masses and speeds, pick a bumper, and launch.
Look at the momentum bars. The total before and the total after are the same.
Now look at the energy bars. Kinetic energy was not all kept. Where do you think it went?
You are riding along with the center of mass. From here the two momenta are equal and opposite, and they add up to zero.
Type the speeds you expect after the collision, then launch and compare.
Glider A never catches glider B, so they never collide.
This is the crumple zone bench. A glider hits a force sensor through a nose you choose, and the graph shows force over time.
The shaded area under the curve is the impulse. It always equals the glider's change in momentum.
This glider bounced back. Its change in momentum is bigger than a glider that just stops, so the impulse is bigger too.
It bottomed out. The crumple zone ran out of room, and the stiff steel behind it took the rest of the hit.
Each spec sets a force limit and a crush length. One of them cannot be met. Find it and show why with numbers.
Spec met.
Every run you record lands here. If momentum is conserved, your points fall on the dashed line.
Set the masses and speeds, pick a bumper, then press Launch. Drag a glider to move its start spot.
Compare the Before and After rows, then record the run for the Notebook.
Nothing is moving. Give a glider some speed.
No collision: A never catches B.
No collision: a glider reached an end stop before A caught B.
Type both predictions to unlock Launch.
Pick a nose and press Launch. The graph shows the force on the glider while it touches the sensor.
Read the peak force and the impulse, then record the run for the Notebook.
Record runs on the two benches, then use the plots and tables to answer the questions.
Notebook full. Copy and clear a table to keep going.
